recommendations.title: Confirm lunch rush sell-through by 2:30PM; adjust 3rd batch by up to ±6 chickens based on sales pace
recommendations.outcome: Midday and afternoon production will better match actual demand, lowering waste and maintaining a full-feeling case.
recommendations.content:
Check actual rotisserie sales from 12-2PM. If sales fall short of midday volume plan (90 units), reduce the 3PM batch by up to 6 chickens. If sales exceed plan, increase by up to 6 chickens. This ensures you react in real time to true customer demand, optimizing inventory and reducing food waste while still presenting a plentiful case to drive traffic.

insights.title: Peak batch: 58% of today's rotisserie output falls into 2nd and 3rd shifts (lunch/afternoon rush)
insights.content: Lunch and afternoon shifts (12PM & 3PM) together produce 90 chickens—58% of total daily volume. This matches sales concentration before 6PM. It supports the recommendation to closely monitor midday demand and adjust afternoon batch up or down, preventing overproduction and waste.

insights.title: Morning batch is frontloaded, but evening production is cut by over 50% vs. midday high
insights.content: First batch (9AM) is set to 25 chickens to ensure full shelves at open. Last batch (6PM) is just 21—a 54% drop from the peak. This keeps the case looking stocked but sharply limits evening waste, supporting the rationale for targeted reductions.

insights.title: Batch 2 volume exceeds batch 1 by 44%—focus operational checks at midday
insights.content: Midday production ramps up to 42 chickens vs. 25 at open—a 44% increase. This highlights midday as the prime window for sales opportunity and risk of waste if demand misaligns, supporting the need to validate sell-through and possibly adjust next batch.
